content.jointProblem: Can site-specific statistical or one-class baselines detect meaningful deviations in ProtoSense's Modbus TCP and BACnet/IP traffic without labelled attacks, while keeping operational alert burden manageable and explaining deviations to plant managers? The first experiment would test transfer to BACnet and ArmaturaSec's hardware using temporally held-out site captures and controlled bench scenarios, measuring false-alert burden, scenario detection, explanation usefulness, and resource overhead without assuming published results will transfer.

rationale.text: Kiss has directly relevant experience developing calibration and incremental-update methods for operational SCADA anomaly detection without labelled attack data.

sources.quote: The project developed threshold calibration procedures for detectors operating without labelled attack data
enabling validation under real traffic conditions.

rationale.text: Her Modbus work provides a concrete starting point for site-specific baselines based on register-level timing, values, and command sequences.

sources.quote: For each register address, empirical distributions of inter-request intervals, payload values, and function code sequences were estimated using kernel density estimation

rationale.text: She has investigated threshold calibration with unlabelled operational data, directly relevant to the company's deployment false-positive problem.

sources.quote: proposes a post-hoc calibration procedure using a small set of unlabelled operational data.

rationale.text: Her research addresses online adaptation to process changes with bounded detector memory, offering a candidate approach for long-running appliances.

sources.quote: Concept drift induced by a planned process reconfiguration was detected as a persistent anomaly episode
Memory footprint per detector instance was under 120 KB.

rationale.text: She has measured detector optimisation on constrained ARM hardware, providing relevant deployment experience rather than evidence of compatibility with ProtoSense itself.

sources.quote: A combined 8-bit quantised, 25%-pruned model achieved inference at 0.9 ms per 10-second window on an ARM Cortex-A7 target

rationale.text: Her group can support controlled Modbus experiments and long-term capture, complementing the company's hardware bench.

sources.quote: The group operates a dedicated ICS testbed equipped with Siemens-compatible PLCs, Modbus/TCP and DNP3 traffic generators, and packet capture infrastructure for long-term dataset collection.

constraints.text: Training and operational calibration must not depend on confirmed attack examples; the archives should be treated as unlabelled, not guaranteed clean.

sources.quote: we have zero examples of malicious traffic
so if they were compromised they would not know.

constraints.text: The scope must cover both Modbus TCP and BACnet/IP and learn site-specific behaviour rather than rely solely on public-dataset performance.

sources.quote: ProtoSense: passive protocol inspection module for Modbus TCP and BACnet/IP traffic
What we actually need is something that learns what normal looks like on a specific site

constraints.text: Alert thresholds and explanations must be usable by plant staff; excessive false positives are an adoption-blocking failure mode.

sources.quote: it flagged so many false positives in real deployments that clients started switching the alerts off.
we can explain to a plant manager in plain language.

constraints.text: Deployment must support local inference in the existing embedded environment, with packet-forwarding impact explicitly tested; the planned processor variant cannot be assumed available.

sources.quote: we have the hardware to run inference on-device
Embedded Linux (custom Yocto build)
with a dedicated security processor to support on-device anomaly detection without affecting packet forwarding latency.

constraints.text: The work plan must fit one to two part-time company engineers and arrange NDA-governed access to archives, hardware, and firmware.

sources.quote: We can dedicate one to two engineers part-time to a collaborative project
with access to our traffic archives, our hardware bench, and our existing firmware codebase under NDA.

constraints.text: Use of the research group's testbed requires a data-sharing agreement.

sources.quote: Her group's testbed capacity is available to industrial partners under a data-sharing agreement.

risks: No supplied publication demonstrates BACnet detection. Transfer from Modbus, DNP3, or other protocols is unvalidated; BACnet feature extraction and controlled scenarios must be tested in the first experiment.
Published hardware measurements concern other targets and workloads. ProtoSense throughput, memory limits, and the availability of the planned security processor remain unconfirmed.

Historical captures may contain undetected compromise or omit important operating modes. Baseline contamination and seasonal or maintenance-related changes could cause missed anomalies or persistent false alerts.
Anomalous traffic is not necessarily malicious, and attacks that resemble normal operations may escape detection. Bench scenarios cannot establish real-world attack coverage.
Plain-language explanations have not been validated with ArmaturaSec's plant managers; technically meaningful features may still produce unactionable alerts.

Researcher availability and allocated team capacity are unknown. Budget, delivery schedule, and integration ownership are also unspecified, creating execution risk despite open joint-project willingness.
Automatic adaptation could absorb malicious behaviour into the baseline unless update gating and operator review are tested.
questions: What availability and team capacity can Kiss commit, and what budget, milestones, and delivery dates can both parties support?
Which ProtoSense hardware is available now, and what CPU, RAM, storage, traffic-rate, inference-time, and packet-forwarding limits must the prototype meet?
How much Modbus and BACnet traffic is available per site, and do captures include timestamps, parsed fields, operational-mode histories, maintenance records, and known configuration changes?
Do existing client permissions cover university access, derived datasets, and controlled replay? What NDA, data-sharing, retention, IP, and publication terms are required?
What false-alert rate per site or day and detection delay would operators accept, and who can review alerts and judge explanation usefulness during the pilot?
Can the first experiment include BACnet-capable equipment or simulation, representative benign changes, and safely injected attack scenarios isolated from production?
How will training, calibration, and evaluation be separated chronologically, and how will uncertain archive contamination be assessed without treating all unlabelled events as benign?
Who will own firmware integration, threshold approval, baseline-update authorisation, rollback, and long-term maintenance after the research prototype?
